answer: Proof-of-stake bonding makes sybil identities expensive. Each AI agent must lock collateral before it can take jobs or vote on results. If an agent is caught colluding, its stake is slashed, so a fake identity loses real capital. Splitting a plume of attackers across many wallets does not dilute the cost, since every identity needs its own bond. Near the nadir of market trust, a spiral of slashing can make attacks unprofitable faster than they can scale.
